title: Runtime adapter escalation playbook & ownership ledger
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, operational playbook for ownership and escalation of runtime adapter incidents and control-plane boundary violations. Focus is on actionable steps for oncall engineers and service owners: triage, containment, owner handoff, cross-region fallbacks, and postmortem triggers. This document doubles as an ownership ledger so we have one canonical place to check who owns which adapter surface and the immediate escalation contact chain.

Scope:
- Control plane pieces covered: API gateway, Orchestrator (control-plane), Runtime Adapters (region-specific GPU pools, model-specific adapters, quantized-runtime shim).
- Multi-region considerations: regional failover, global routing policies, and data-plane vs control-plane isolation.
- Not covered: infra-level hardware failures (SRE runbooks exist separately), billing/quotas.

Quick summary (one-liner):
If a request path is failing in production, follow the triage checklist, identify the failing surface (gateway | orchestrator | adapter), contain via automated policies (route to fallback), then escalate along the ledger.

Ownership ledger (canonical):
- API Gateway (edge + routing): owner: Liam Chen, primary pager: liam@redwood.ai, backup: Priya Kapoor. Responsibilities: tenant ingress auth, route selection, request shaping, rate-limits.
- Orchestrator / Control Plane: owner: Ava Martinez, primary pager: ava@redwood.ai, backup: Noah Brooks. Responsibilities: model selection, rollout decision, global policy enforcement, canary rollouts.
- Runtime Adapters (region-us-east-1): owner: Noah Brooks, pager: noah@redwood.ai, backup: Sofia Reyes. Responsibilities: adapter health, capacity, kernel selection heuristics.
- Runtime Adapters (region-eu-west-1): owner: Sofia Reyes, pager: sofia@redwood.ai, backup: Liam Chen.
- Quantized Shim & Kernel Selector: owner: Priya Kapoor, pager: priya@redwood.ai, backup: Ava Martinez.
- Incident commander fallback (when owner unreachable): eng-platform-lead oncall (escalate via PagerDuty escalation policy).

Escalation matrix (severity-driven):
- Sev1 (global outage / large customer impact): immediate page to all primary owners + engineering manager. Lead: incident commander from eng-platform oncall. Actions: open incident channel, triage, enable global fallback routes, temporarily disable rolling canary, trigger immediate postmortem. SLA: acknowledge < 5min, mitigation plan < 15min.
- Sev2 (regional outage / degraded): page regional owner and orchestrator oncall. Actions: route traffic to healthy region where feasible, enable limited capacity degradation, coordinate customer comms. SLA: ack < 15min, mitigation < 60min.
- Sev3 (minor errors / perf regressions): log + slack notify owners, investigate during business hours. SLA: ack by next business day.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm impact and scope: Is this single-customer, single-region, or global? Check dashboards: per-route latency, error rate, token failure codes.
2) Identify failing surface: 
   - API Gateway errors (4xx auth, 5xx routing): check gateway logs and request-id chain.
   - Orchestrator errors (policy reject, model mismatch): check decision logs and rollout flags.
   - Adapter errors (OOMs, kernel crash, model mismatch): check adapter logs, container restarts, GPU metrics.
3) Apply containment: Enable pre-configured fallback policy: route to compatible model variant or downgrade quantization, or send to dedicated capacity if reserved.
4) If containment successful, notify impacted owners and start incident. If not, escalate immediately to Sev1 path.

Oncall run steps by surface (practical):
- API Gateway:
  - Verify route table for the tenant, check token validation chain, replay failing request (with sanitized PII) to debug mode.
  - Temporarily mark route as degraded and shift traffic to edge-cached responses where applicable.
  - If misrouting due to config drift, rollback recent route config commit (note: coordinate with SRE for traffic shaping).
- Orchestrator:
  - Inspect decision logs for rollout flags and candidate model ids. If a canary is the cause, flip rollback flag to previous stable version.
  - If policy mismatch (e.g., region-specific pinning not honored), check control-plane mutations and audit log for last writer.
- Runtime Adapter:
  - Check adapter health endpoint, GPU memory, kernel crashes. If adapter process keeps restarting, capture stack traces and core dumps.
  - If quantization-specific failures observed, shift request to the non-quantized variant (a built-in fallback).
  - For capacity exhaustion, trigger autoscale playbook or drain non-critical workloads.

Multi-region fallback patterns (decision rules):
- Prefer same-region first for latency-sensitive tenants. Use weighted routing with safety threshold: if 99th percentile latency > threshold for region for 2 consecutive minutes, shift 30% of traffic to secondary region as experiment, then 100% if stable.
- Respect data residency flags: If tenant has residency constraints, do not shift outside allowed regions — instead enable degrade-to-cache mode or offer scheduled retry.
- Model consistency: When routing across regions, prefer identical model version + quantization profile; if unavailable, prefer higher-fidelity model in target region rather than lower-fidelity.

Example incident (short):
- What happened: sudden increase in adapter OOMs in us-east-1 after a quantized kernel rollout.
- Immediate action: oncall shifted traffic to eu-west-1 compatible adapter, flipped orchestrator rollout flag to previous kernel, scaled up reserved capacity, opened incident channel.
- Postmortem takeaways: gating for kernel memory footprint tests missing, introduce pre-rollout memory profiling harness and add automated canary with synthetic load.

Template for incident channel opener (copy-paste):
[INCIDENT] title: Runtime adapter OOMs in us-east-1 - impact: 42% requests 5xx - severity: Sev2
Initial triage: AVL checks - gateway healthy, orchestrator flagged recent kernel rollout, adapter processes restarting every 30s.
Owners: Noah Brooks (adapter owner), Ava Martinez (orchestrator), Liam Chen (gateway)
Mitigation: shift to eu-west-1, rollback kernel, scale up reserved pool

Post-incident governance items (short list):
- Add memory profiling to pre-release suite for kernel shims.
- Create runbook for safe cross-region traffic shifting with audit logs.
- Update ownership ledger when adapter teams rotate (owner change checklist below).

Owner change checklist (when team rotates):
- New owner must: 1) be added to PagerDuty rotation; 2) have access to adapter logs and region consoles; 3) run a short handover session (30m) recorded and uploaded to Confluence; 4) verify ownership ledger entry.

Open questions / action items (todo):
- Define explicit rollback window thresholds for canary kernels (Priya to propose by 2025-01-20).
- Add synthetic cross-region latency test to Canary CI (SRE + eng-platform pairing).
- Decide on single canonical place for adapter contract JSON (Confluence link above is current but may move to git).

Notes and references:
- See linked artifacts for related specs and PRs.
- For infra-level hardware failures see: shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/hardware-failure-runbook.json

If you find an ownership mismatch in this ledger, please open a tiny PR on this doc and ping the platform leads — we aim to keep this file small and operational.
